title: Remedies in action: cost, institutions, and nonlegal enforcement
shortTitle: Remedies in action: cost, institutions, and nonlegal e…
summary: The practical value of an entitlement depends on the cost and means of enforcing it.
notes: Litigation costs, attorney fees, delay, collectability, and bargaining position can separate legal damages from net recovery. The text considers business reputation, repeat dealings, and private dispute institutions as additional enforcement mechanisms. Macaulay’s business observations, Galanter’s repeat-player analysis, Mentschikoff’s arbitration discussion, and Bernstein’s private-ordering work approach different parts of this problem. A source’s descriptive observation is distinct from a recommendation to substitute a private system for courts.
